articles.title: Bhagwandutt S.N.K. High School, Bandwar
articles.metaTitle: S.N.K. High School Bandwar (Est. 1942) - History & Info
articles.metaDescription: Discover Bhagwandutt S.N.K. High School, Bandwar (Est. 1942). The oldest school in Begusarai, Bihar. UDISE Code: 10201013302. Read history & current status.
articles.subtitle: The village's oldest school — established in 1942 as a Sanskrit gurukul
articles.summary: Established in 1942 by Pandit Taradutt Pathak, S.N.K. High School is the oldest educational institution in Bandwar, Begusarai. Originally a free Sanskrit gurukul, it now operates as a government secondary school (Classes 9-10) with UDISE code 10201013302.

photos.caption: The main building of Bhagwandutt S.N.K. High School, Bandwar.
photos.imageAlt: Front view of the historic S.N.K. High School building in Bandwar, Begusarai

content.heading: Origins — The 1942 Gurukul
content.text: In 1942, during the final years of British rule, Pandit Taradutt Pathak established a Sanskrit school in memory of his father Pandit Bhagwan Dutt Pathak. It was a traditional gurukul — students came from across Bihar, and education, food, and lodging were all provided free of cost. This was a period when formal schooling was rare in rural Bihar, and the establishment of a free gurukul in a village like Bandwar was an act of considerable ambition. The school's founding predates Indian independence by five years, and it was among the earliest educational institutions in the region.

content.heading: After Independence
content.text: Following India's independence, the school was brought under the Department of Education and became a government secondary school. It continued to serve Bandwar and the surrounding areas of Begusarai for decades. The school's transition from a private gurukul to a government institution mirrored the broader transformation of education in post-independence Bihar — a period in which the state took on the responsibility for schooling that had once been borne by philanthropists and communities.

content.heading: Present Day
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school today serves Classes 9 and 10 with an enrolment of just 12 students — 2 boys and 10 girls. It has 4 teachers, 5 classrooms, a library, and electricity, but no boundary wall and no playground. Like [[gps-paschimibandwar-school|GPS Paschimibandwar]] and several other schools in the village, the school faces the challenges common to rural secondary education in Bihar.

content.heading: Legacy
content.text: The school's history represents both the ambition of Bandwar's founders and the challenges faced by rural secondary education in Bihar. A place that once offered free education to students from across the region now struggles to sustain its enrolment. Students who would once have come to Bandwar for its gurukul now travel to Begusarai, Barauni, or even Patna for their secondary education. And yet the school remains — a quiet witness to the eighty years of educational history that have passed through its gates.

faqs.q: When was S.N.K. High School established?
faqs.a: S.N.K. High School was established in 1942 by Pandit Taradutt Pathak, in memory of his father Pandit Bhagwan Dutt Pathak. It is the oldest educational institution in Bandwar village.

faqs.q: What does 'S.N.K.' stand for?
faqs.a: S.N.K. stands for 'Sanskrit Nagri Kanya' — though in its present form the school is co-educational. The name reflects its origins as a Sanskrit gurukul founded in the memory of Pandit Bhagwan Dutt Pathak.

faqs.q: What is the UDISE code of S.N.K. High School?
faqs.a: The school's UDISE code is 10201013302. It operates under the Bihar Department of Education as a government secondary school serving Classes 9 and 10.

faqs.q: How many students study at S.N.K. High School today?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 12 students — 2 boys and 10 girls — taught by 4 teachers. The low enrolment reflects the wider challenges of rural secondary education in Bihar.

faqs.q: Was S.N.K. High School always a government school?
faqs.a: No — it began in 1942 as a private Sanskrit gurukul, providing free education, food, and lodging to students from across Bihar. After independence, it was brought under the Department of Education and became a government secondary school.

articles.title: UHS +2 Bandwar (Higher Secondary School)
articles.metaDescription: UHS +2 Bandwar is the largest school in the village (Classes 9-12). UDISE Code: 10201008406. Learn about its 601 students, facilities, and educational impact.
articles.subtitle: The village's main higher secondary school — Classes 9 to 12
articles.summary: UHS +2 Bandwar (Upgraded High School +2) is the largest higher secondary school in Bandwar, Begusarai. Established in 1955 (UDISE: 10201008406), it provides education from Class 9 to 12 to 601 students, with a focus on inclusivity.

photos.caption: The main building of UHS +2 Bandwar, the largest school in the village.
photos.imageAlt: UHS Plus 2 Bandwar school building in Begusarai

content.heading: Overview
content.text: UHS +2 Bandwar is the higher secondary school of Bandwar village, established in 1955 as part of Bihar's post-independence expansion of rural education. It holds UDISE code 10201008406 and today offers Classes 9 through 12 with a total enrolment of 601 students — the largest of any school in the village. The school is one of the few government institutions in Bandwar to offer education up to Class 12, and it serves not just Bandwar but also the surrounding panchayats.

content.heading: Enrolment
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school has 315 boys and 286 girls. 394 students are from Other Backward Classes (66%), 99 from Scheduled Castes, and 100 from Muslim families. 524 students — 87% of the school — belong to Below Poverty Line households. This is a striking picture of the village's social fabric, and it reflects the school's role as one of the most inclusive institutions in Bandwar.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school operates from a single pucca block with 8 classrooms, all in good condition. It has 6 toilets each for boys and girls, drinking water, electricity, and internet. It does not, however, have a library, a playground, or a boundary wall. The absence of a library is notable — students preparing for board examinations have no dedicated reading space within the school, and often rely on the [[vaani-vilas-library-bandwar|Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya]] for their reading needs.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 15 teachers — 8 male and 7 female. 14 of them are post-graduates, and 12 hold a B.Ed. or equivalent qualification. The pupil-teacher ratio is roughly 40:1 — above the ideal ratio prescribed by the Right to Education Act, but not unusual for rural secondary schools in Bihar. The school's teaching staff is relatively well-qualified compared to other government schools in the area.

content.heading: Legacy and Challenges
content.text: UHS +2 Bandwar represents both the achievements and the challenges of rural education in Bihar. On the one hand, the school has managed to sustain an enrolment of over 600 students across four classes, and to retain a relatively well-qualified teaching staff. On the other hand, the school has no library, no playground, and no boundary wall — and its pupil-teacher ratio is over 40:1. These are the same challenges that face [[snk-high-school-bandwar|S.N.K. High School]] and the village's primary schools.

faqs.q: What classes does UHS +2 Bandwar offer?
faqs.a: UHS +2 Bandwar offers Classes 9 through 12, making it the only higher secondary school in Bandwar village. It is one of ten schools operating in the village.

faqs.q: How many students study at UHS +2 Bandwar?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 601 students — 315 boys and 286 girls — the largest enrolment of any school in Bandwar. 87% of students belong to Below Poverty Line households.

faqs.q: When was UHS +2 Bandwar established?
faqs.a: UHS +2 Bandwar was established in 1955, as part of Bihar's post-independence expansion of rural education. Its UDISE code is 10201008406.

faqs.q: Does UHS +2 Bandwar have a library?
faqs.a: No — the school does not have a library or a playground. Students often rely on the Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya, the village library on Bandwar Road, for their reading needs.

faqs.q: What is the student-teacher ratio at UHS +2 Bandwar?
faqs.a: The school has 15 teachers for 601 students, giving a pupil-teacher ratio of roughly 40:1 — above the ideal ratio prescribed by the Right to Education Act.

articles.title: MS Bandwar (Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya)
articles.metaTitle: MS Bandwar (Middle School) - Classes 1 to 8 | Begusarai
articles.metaDescription: Government middle school in Bandwar, Begusarai. UDISE: 10201008401. Serving 669 students from Class 1 to 8. View facilities, teachers, and history.
articles.subtitle: The village's main government middle school — Classes 1 to 8
articles.summary: MS Bandwar (Middle School Bandwar) is the main government middle school in Bandwar, Begusarai. Established in 1955 (UDISE: 10201008401), it serves Classes 1 to 8 with 669 students, making it the most inclusive school in the village.

photos.caption: The main building of MS Bandwar (Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya).
photos.imageAlt: Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya Bandwar building in Begusarai

content.heading: Overview
content.text: MS Bandwar — Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya — is the government middle school of Bandwar village. Established in 1955, it serves Classes 1 through 8 and is one of the largest schools in the village, with 669 students on its rolls in the 2025-26 academic year. It is a 'Primary with Upper Primary' school, meaning it educates students from Class 1 all the way to Class 8.

content.heading: Enrolment and Diversity
content.text: The school has 351 boys and 318 girls. Its enrolment is dominated by Other Backward Classes (506 students, 76%), with 118 Scheduled Caste students and 111 Muslim students. 633 students — 95% — belong to Below Poverty Line households. It is a striking picture of the village's social fabric, and it reflects the school's role as one of the most inclusive institutions in Bandwar.

content.heading: Infrastructure
content.text: According to its UDISE+ report, the school runs from 3 pucca building blocks with 8 classrooms. All 8 classrooms, however, need major repair. The boundary wall is pucca but broken. The school does have a library, a playground, electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting — and it received ₹1,00,000 in grants for 2025-26. The [[vaani-vilas-library-bandwar|Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya]] on Bandwar Road supplements the school's own library.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 17 teachers — 7 male and 10 female. 7 hold B.Ed. qualifications and 7 hold D.El.Ed. diplomas. The pupil-teacher ratio is approximately 39:1. The presence of 10 female teachers in a rural government middle school is notable, and reflects the growing presence of women in Bihar's teaching profession.

content.heading: Bridging Primary and Secondary
content.text: As the only government school in Bandwar offering the full Class 1–8 range, MS Bandwar plays a central role in the village's educational pipeline. Students who complete Class 8 here move on to [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]] or [[snk-high-school-bandwar|S.N.K. High School]] for their secondary education.

faqs.q: What classes does MS Bandwar offer?
faqs.a: MS Bandwar offers Classes 1 through 8, making it the only government school in the village to cover the full primary and upper primary range.

faqs.q: How many students study at MS Bandwar?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 669 students — 351 boys and 318 girls — one of the largest middle schools in the area.

faqs.q: When was MS Bandwar established?
faqs.a: MS Bandwar was established in 1955, the same year as UHS +2 Bandwar. Its UDISE code is 10201008401.

faqs.q: What is the condition of MS Bandwar's classrooms?
faqs.a: The school runs from 3 pucca building blocks with 8 classrooms. All 8 classrooms, however, need major repair, and the boundary wall is pucca but broken.

faqs.q: Does MS Bandwar have a library and playground?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has both a library and a playground, along with electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting.

articles.title: GPS Paschimibandwar (Government Primary School)
articles.metaTitle: GPS Paschimibandwar - Primary School West Bandwar
articles.metaDescription: Government Primary School Paschimibandwar in Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1952. UDISE Code: 10201008402. Serving Classes 1-5.
articles.subtitle: Primary school in West Bandwar — established 1952
articles.summary: GPS Paschimibandwar (Government Primary School, West Bandwar) is a government primary school in the western part of Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1952 with UDISE code 10201008402, it serves Classes 1 through 5 with 150 students.

photos.caption: The main building of GPS Paschimibandwar in West Bandwar.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: GPS Paschimibandwar is a government primary school in the western part of Bandwar, close to the embankment that runs along the [[burhi-gandak|Burhi Gandak]]. Established in 1952 with UDISE code 10201008402, it is one of the oldest schools in the village. The school's name reflects its location: 'Paschimi' means 'western' in Hindi, and the school serves the families living in the western part of the village.

content.heading: Enrolment
content.text: As per the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 150 students — 83 boys and 67 girls. 118 students are from Other Backward Classes, 27 from Scheduled Castes, and 29 from Muslim families. 126 students — 84% — belong to Below Poverty Line households.

content.heading: Infrastructure
content.text: The school operates from 3 pucca building blocks with 7 classrooms — 5 in good condition and 2 in need of major repair. It has a playground, drinking water, electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting. It does not have a library, and the boundary wall is pucca but broken.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 9 teachers — 4 male and 5 female. Only 1 holds a B.Ed. qualification, and 5 teachers are below graduate level. The school received ₹30,000 in grants for 2025-26.

content.heading: Context
content.text: GPS Paschimibandwar is one of three government primary schools in Bandwar — the others being [[gps-mohanpur-kanya-school|GPS Mohanpur Kanya]] and [[gps-bandwar-musahri-school|GPS Bandwar Musahri]]. Together, these three schools serve the bulk of the village's primary-age children.

faqs.q: When was GPS Paschimibandwar established?
faqs.a: GPS Paschimibandwar was established in 1952 — one of the oldest schools in Bandwar village. Its UDISE code is 10201008402.

faqs.q: How many students study at GPS Paschimibandwar?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 150 students — 83 boys and 67 girls. 84% of students belong to Below Poverty Line households.

faqs.q: Does GPS Paschimibandwar have a playground?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has a playground, along with drinking water, electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting.

faqs.q: Why is the school called 'Paschimibandwar'?
faqs.a: 'Paschimi' means 'western' in Hindi. The school is located in the western part of Bandwar village.

articles.summary: GPS Mohanpur Kanya is the girls-only government primary school serving Bandwar panchayat in Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1956 with UDISE code 10201009102, it serves Classes 1 through 5 exclusively for girls, with an enrolment of 74 students.

photos.caption: The main building of GPS Mohanpur Kanya, the girls-only primary school.
photos.imageAlt: GPS Mohanpur Kanya girls primary school building

content.heading: Overview
content.text: GPS Mohanpur Kanya is the girls-only government primary school serving the Bandwar panchayat area. Established in 1956 with UDISE code 10201009102, it provides primary education exclusively to girls from Class 1 to Class 5.

content.heading: The School
content.text: According to its UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school has 74 girls on its rolls — 47 from Other Backward Classes, 25 from the general category, and 2 each from Scheduled Caste and Muslim families. 69 of the 74 students — 93% — belong to Below Poverty Line households.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school runs from a single pucca block with 6 classrooms — 4 in good condition and 2 in need of major repair. It has a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps, but no playground and no boundary wall.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 8 teachers — 3 male and 5 female. Only 1 holds a B.Ed. qualification and 1 holds a D.El.Ed. diploma. 4 teachers are below graduate level. The school's instructional days for 2025-26 were 236.

content.heading: Girls' Education in Bandwar
content.text: The existence of a dedicated girls' school in Bandwar reflects a broader shift in attitudes towards girls' education in the village. Today, girls outnumber boys at several schools in the village — including [[snk-high-school-bandwar|S.N.K. High School]] and [[nps-kunjartol-wd-9|NPS Kunjartol WD-9]].

faqs.q: Is GPS Mohanpur Kanya a girls-only school?
faqs.a: Yes — GPS Mohanpur Kanya is the girls-only government primary school serving Bandwar panchayat.

faqs.q: When was GPS Mohanpur Kanya established?
faqs.a: GPS Mohanpur Kanya was established in 1956. Its UDISE code is 10201009102.

faqs.q: How many girls study at GPS Mohanpur Kanya?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 74 girls on its rolls. 93% belong to Below Poverty Line households.

faqs.q: Does GPS Mohanpur Kanya have a library?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has a library, along with drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps.

articles.title: GPS Bandwar Musahri (Government Primary School)
articles.metaTitle: GPS Bandwar Musahri - Government Primary School
articles.metaDescription: Government primary school in the Musahri tola of Bandwar, Begusarai. Established 1995. UDISE Code: 10201008403. Serving 196 students.
articles.subtitle: Primary school in the Musahri tola — established 1995
articles.summary: GPS Bandwar Musahri is a government primary school in the Musahri tola of Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1995 with UDISE code 10201008403, it serves Classes 1 through 5 with an enrolment of 196 students — the majority from Scheduled Caste and Below Poverty Line households.

photos.caption: The main building of GPS Bandwar Musahri in the Musahri tola.
photos.imageAlt: Government Primary School Bandwar Musahri building in Begusarai

content.heading: Overview
content.text: GPS Bandwar Musahri is a government primary school in the Musahri tola of Bandwar. Established in 1995 with UDISE code 10201008403, it is the largest primary school in the village, with 196 students on its rolls in the 2025-26 academic year.

content.heading: A Mahadalit-Majority School
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, 172 of the school's 196 students — 88% — belong to Scheduled Caste families. 162 students belong to Below Poverty Line households. The presence of a well-enrolled primary school in the Musahri tola reflects the village's commitment to ensuring that education reaches all communities.

content.heading: Enrolment
content.text: The school has 103 boys and 93 girls — a notable gender balance. Class sizes range from 24 (Class IV) to 68 (Class I). It has 4 classrooms, all in good condition, and 2 functional toilets.

content.heading: Facilities and Grants
content.text: The school has a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps. It received ₹75,000 in grants for 2025-26. It does not have a playground or a boundary wall. The presence of a library is notable — students in the Musahri tola have limited access to books at home, and the school's library is often their first exposure to a reading culture.

content.heading: Context
content.text: GPS Bandwar Musahri is one of three government primary schools in Bandwar — the others being [[gps-paschimibandwar-school|GPS Paschimibandwar]] and [[gps-mohanpur-kanya-school|GPS Mohanpur Kanya]]. Students from GPS Bandwar Musahri move on to [[ms-bandwar-middle-school|MS Bandwar]] for upper primary education.

faqs.q: When was GPS Bandwar Musahri established?
faqs.a: GPS Bandwar Musahri was established in 1995 — more than four decades after the village's other primary schools. Its UDISE code is 10201008403.

faqs.q: How many students study at GPS Bandwar Musahri?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 196 students — 103 boys and 93 girls — making it the largest primary school in Bandwar.

faqs.q: What is the Musahri tola?
faqs.a: The Musahri tola is a locality within Bandwar village, historically home to families from Scheduled Caste and Mahadalit communities.

faqs.q: Does GPS Bandwar Musahri have a playground?
faqs.a: No — the school does not have a playground or a boundary wall. It does have a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, ramps, and 2 functional toilets.

content.text: NPS Kunjartol WD-9 is a government primary school in the Kunjartol tola of Bandwar, Ward 9. Established in 2007 with UDISE code 10201013301, it serves Classes 1 through 5 with 327 students — the second-largest primary school in the village.

content.heading: A Diverse Enrolment
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school has 152 boys and 175 girls — one of the few schools in Bandwar where girls outnumber boys. 265 students are from Other Backward Classes, 186 from Muslim families, and 60 from Scheduled Castes. 321 students — 98% — belong to Below Poverty Line households.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school runs from a single pucca building block with 3 classrooms, all in good condition. It has a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, ramps, and medical checkup facilities — but no playground and no boundary wall.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 14 teachers — 10 male and 4 female. 10 hold D.El.Ed. diplomas, 2 hold B.Ed. qualifications, and 7 are graduates. The pupil-teacher ratio is roughly 23:1 — one of the better ratios among Bandwar's schools.

content.heading: Context
content.text: NPS Kunjartol WD-9 is the newest of Bandwar's government primary schools, and its enrolment has grown rapidly since its founding. Along with [[gps-bandwar-musahri-school|GPS Bandwar Musahri]] and [[gps-paschimibandwar-school|GPS Paschimibandwar]], it serves the bulk of the village's primary-age children.

faqs.q: What does 'NPS' stand for in NPS Kunjartol WD-9?
faqs.a: 'NPS' stands for 'New Primary School' — a designation used by the Bihar government for schools established under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.

faqs.q: How many students study at NPS Kunjartol WD-9?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 327 students — 152 boys and 175 girls — the second-largest primary school in Bandwar.

faqs.q: Where is NPS Kunjartol WD-9 located?
faqs.a: The school is in the Kunjartol tola of Bandwar village, Ward 9.

faqs.q: Does NPS Kunjartol WD-9 offer medical checkups?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has medical checkup facilities, along with a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps.

articles.summary: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir is a private unaided primary school in Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 2015 with UDISE code 10201008405, it offers Classes 1 through 8 in Hindi medium.

photos.imageAlt: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir school building Bandwar

content.heading: Overview
content.text: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir is a private unaided school in Bandwar, established in 2015 with UDISE code 10201008405. It offers primary education (Classes 1–5) with upper primary classes (6–8), and is one of only two private schools in the village — the other being [[st-paul-school-bandwar|St. Paul School]].

content.heading: Why It Matters
content.text: Until 2015, most schools in Bandwar were government-run. The opening of Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir gave parents a private alternative. The school's enrolment of 151 students — 111 from Other Backward Classes, 34 from the general category — reflects the demand for private schooling in rural Bihar.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school operates from a rented building with 14 classrooms, all in good condition. It has a library, playground, drinking water, electricity, internet, medical checkups, and ramps. Furniture availability, however, is minimal.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 15 teachers — 7 male and 8 female. 11 of the 15 teachers do not hold a formal teaching qualification (neither B.Ed. nor D.El.Ed.). Only 1 holds a D.El.Ed. diploma. This is a common pattern among low-cost private schools in rural India.

content.heading: Context
content.text: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir is one of two private schools in Bandwar, and one of three schools in the village offering the full Class 1–8 range (along with [[ms-bandwar-middle-school|MS Bandwar]] and [[st-paul-school-bandwar|St. Paul School]]).

faqs.q: When was Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir established?
faqs.a: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir was established in 2015 — one of the first private schools in Bandwar. Its UDISE code is 10201008405.

faqs.q: What classes does Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir offer?
faqs.a: The school offers Classes 1 through 8 — primary with upper primary.

faqs.q: How many students study at Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 151 students — 84 boys and 67 girls.

faqs.q: Do teachers at Adharsh Vikash have formal teaching qualifications?
faqs.a: Most do not — 11 of the school's 15 teachers hold neither a B.Ed. nor a D.El.Ed. qualification.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: St. Paul School is a private unaided English-medium school in Bandwar, established in 2015 with UDISE code 10201008404. It offers Classes 1 through 8 and is one of the only two private schools in the village — the other being [[adharsh-vikash-vidhya-mandir|Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir]].

content.heading: A Different Enrolment
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, St. Paul School has 209 students — 149 boys and 60 girls. Only 15 students (7%) belong to Below Poverty Line households, compared to 87–98% in the village's government schools. 62 students are from the general category.

content.heading: Infrastructure
content.text: The school has 11 classrooms (8 in good condition), a private pucca building, a library, an ICT lab, drinking water, electricity, internet, medical checkups, and ramps. It does not have a playground. The school received formal recognition for its primary classes in 2017 and for upper primary in 2020.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 14 teachers — 11 male and 3 female. Only 2 hold B.Ed. qualifications; 5 teachers have no formal teaching qualification. This is consistent with the wider pattern of private unaided schools in rural Bihar.

content.heading: A Contrast With Government Schools
content.text: The differences between St. Paul School and Bandwar's government schools are stark. Where [[ms-bandwar-middle-school|MS Bandwar]] has 95% BPL students, St. Paul has just 7%. Where [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]] has a pupil-teacher ratio of 40:1, St. Paul's is closer to 15:1.

faqs.q: What is the medium of instruction at St. Paul School?
faqs.a: St. Paul School's medium of instruction is primarily English, with Hindi as a secondary language.

faqs.q: When was St. Paul School established?
faqs.a: St. Paul School was established in 2015 — one of the first private schools in Bandwar. Its UDISE code is 10201008404.

faqs.q: How many students study at St. Paul School?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 209 students — 149 boys and 60 girls.

faqs.q: Does St. Paul School have an ICT lab?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has an ICT (Information and Communication Technology) lab, along with a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and medical checkups.

articles.title: Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya (Village Library)
articles.metaTitle: Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya - Village Library | Bandwar
articles.metaDescription: The historic village library of Bandwar (Est. 1945). Inaugurated in 2025 by MP Rakesh Sinha. Features Wi-Fi, seed library, and reading rooms. Visit the digital portal.
articles.subtitle: The village library on Bandwar Road — established 1945
articles.summary: Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya (वाणी विलास पुस्तकालय) is the historic village library of Bandwar, established in 1945. Its new building, funded by MPLAD and Panchayat, was inaugurated in 2025 by MP Rakesh Sinha, offering Wi-Fi, a seed library, and modern reading spaces.

photos.imageAlt: Wooden cabinets filled with books at Bandwar village library

content.heading: Overview
content.text: Standing on Bandwar Road near the [[shaheed-dwar|Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar]], the library occupies a single-storey white building with a red iron entrance gate. Inside, numbered wooden cabinets and open bookshelves hold Hindi literature, Bengali works, Islamic texts, and reference material.

content.heading: History and Origin
content.text: The library was established on 5 November 1945. Muktinath Singh donated the land for the library building and, together with Girija Singh, supported the initiative for its development. The current building's approximately ₹30 lakh construction cost was supported by ₹15 lakh from the MPLAD fund associated with Rakesh Sinha and ₹15 lakh from Bandwar Gram Panchayat.

content.heading: Services & Facilities
content.text: The library is more than just a reading room. It offers Book Lending (Hindi, Bengali, Islamic texts), Free Wi-Fi & Workspace for students, Workshops & Classes (from spoken word poetry to digital literacy), Community Events (storytelling evenings, harvest festivals), a Children's Corner, and a unique Seed Library where villagers can borrow seeds, grow gardens, and return seeds at harvest.

content.heading: The Reading Area
content.text: A large wooden table and black metal chairs form the heart of the reading room, seating around a dozen readers. Framed portraits of national leaders, including Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, line the walls. The room is especially valued during school examination season.

content.heading: Present Day
content.text: Run daily by the वाणी विलास पुस्तकालय committee, the library welcomes students and older residents as an active part of village life. It carries forward the legacy of its late founders. You can explore more on their official website: https://vanivilaspushtakalya.netlify.app

faqs.q: When was Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya established?
faqs.a: The library was established on 5 November 1945. However, its current building was inaugurated much later on 5 September 2025.

faqs.q: Who built the current building of Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya?
faqs.a: The land was donated by Muktinath Singh. The construction of the current building cost approximately ₹30 lakh, funded by ₹15 lakh from the MPLAD fund and ₹15 lakh from Bandwar Gram Panchayat.

faqs.q: What services does the library offer?
faqs.a: The library offers book lending, free Wi-Fi, workshops, community events, a children's corner, and a unique seed library for farmers.

faqs.q: Who inaugurated the current building?
faqs.a: The current building was inaugurated by Rajya Sabha MP Rakesh Sinha on 5 September 2025 (Teachers' Day).

faqs.q: Where is the library located?
faqs.a: It is located on Bandwar Road, near the Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar. The official website is https://vanivilaspushtakalya.netlify.app.
